newsitem.title: INDIA: India tribal guerrillas threaten more violence.
newsitem.headline: India tribal guerrillas threaten more violence.

text.p: A tribal guerrilla group involved in recent bombings in the northeast Indian state of Assam has threatened more violence if the government does not call for talks to meet its demand for a homeland.

"Violence will be the order of the day and Assam will continue to burn unless the government initiates negotiations at the earliest," Hagnama Basumtary, a BLTF leader, said in a statement issued late on Saturday.
The Bodo Liberation Tigers' Force (BLTF) has claimed responsibility for a series of bomb attacks on bridges, roads and a train in the state in the past week.
But the group denied responsibility for killings of at least 30 people in the state in the past week.
On Monday, more than 400 passengers escaped unhurt when BLTF guerrillas set off a remote-control bomb on a rail track in the state rich in tea and oil.
BLTF is one of the several guerrilla groups fighting in the hilly northeastern region for homelands or independence.
More than one thousand people have been killed in violence linked to a movement for a separate Bodo province since 1985.
BLTF is fighting for an ethnic homeland for around 600,000 Bodo tribespeople, who say the ruling Assam government has deprived them of social, political and economic rights.

Bodo guerrillas have their camps in the foothills of southern Bhutan and accuse Bengali-speaking Hindu immigrants of encroaching on their traditional homeland in Assam. A small Bodo offshoot is fighting for independence.
In December last year, BLTF claimed responsibility for a train bombing that killed at least 30 people.
Police and government officials say at least 45 people have been killed by tribal militants in the state in the past 15 days.
Bodo guerrillas shot dead 13 Bengali-speaking Hindu settlers in Assam's Nalbari district in a night attack on Friday.

Seven people were killed and eight injured on Thursday when a bomb exploded on a train track in the state's North Lakahimpur district, about 200 km (120 miles) east of the region's largest city Guwahati.
Police suspected the involvement of the separatist United Liberation Front of Asom (ULFA) in the blast.
Bodo guerrillas of the National Democratic Front of Bodoland on Tuesday killed 12 Hindus, executing six after tying them to a tree.
